cases.note: A PRESENT 0-byte base is a parse failure, not an absence: JsonReader.beginObject hits EOF at GoApiSnapshot.java:215 (EOFException under IOException). Attacks any empty-file -> missing_base or -> parsed-empty conflation.
Whitespace-only bytes still reach beginObject and fail at EOF (GoApiSnapshot.java:215). Byte count is nonzero so this cannot masquerade as an empty file.

Truncated mid-object: beginObject and the NAME peek succeed, then the bucket value ends at EOF (Gson MalformedJsonException, an IOException, inside the loop at :216-222). Syntax corrupt INSIDE the object, not merely an absent shape.
Missing ':' after a name: strict Gson (bundled gson-2.13.2) throws MalformedJsonException expecting a colon; the document never yields a usable top-level object.

Empty top-level array still fails beginObject (:215, Expected BEGIN_OBJECT but was BEGIN_ARRAY); emptiness does not make it skippable. Model note: the Java exception is IllegalStateException (RuntimeException), not IOException — the model's UnreadableError is the API-level rejection, not an exception-class claim.
Valid JSON scalar bearing a real bucket name: 'all' as a STRING is still not an object; beginObject fails at :215. Guards against any name-sniffing shortcut that reads bytes instead of structure.
Bare NUMBER token at top level: beginObject fails at :215 (Expected BEGIN_OBJECT but was NUMBER). Same API-level rejection class as the array case.

JSON null is a PRESENT document, not a missing file and not an empty object: beginObject fails at :215 on the NULL token. Sharpest parse-vs-missing boundary: null bytes decode fine, they are simply the wrong shape.

Single 0xFF byte (raw_b64 of b'\xff'): even under the Java InputStreamReader's REPLACE decoding this is U+FFFD, not BEGIN_OBJECT — beginObject fails at :215. Model rejects at strict UTF-8 decode; same failure class via a different step.

raw_b64 of b'{"a\x01ll": {}}': raw control char U+0001 inside a quoted member name. Strict Gson 2.13.2 rejects unescaped control characters in strings; Python strict mode agrees. A lenient reader would have surfaced bucket 'a\x01ll' — it must not.

A selectable exact diff must NOT redeem a corrupt base: the runtime path would feed the same unreadable bytes through JsonPatchApplier(jsonFile) (getDerivedByteProviderPush callback, :133-144), so the failure propagates. Selection must error, never emit exact_diff over a base it could not read.

The parsed-zero counterpart to missing_base: a present, VALID '{}' base (3 materialized bytes) yields zero matching buckets with source 'unpatched_base_file' — never null base, never missing_base — and the exact diff still selects. Size pins a real file distinct from the 0-byte unreadable case.

Empty readable root: getApiSnapshotFile returns null (:168-177) so get() yields GoApiSnapshot.EMPTY (:115, :242). The discriminating key is base_matching_buckets_source==null — a wrongly-synthesized parsed-empty base would emit 'unpatched_base_file' and status base_only. selected_patch must stay null (absent), not 0 (patch-0 byte source).
A populated patchverdiffs/ (non-diff member) without any base is still missing_base: base lookup precedes the diff scan (:122-126) and 'keepme.txt' never matches the diff name grammar anyway.

A DIRECTORY named go1.21.0.json is not a base file: Application.getDataFileInModule throws FileNotFoundException when the found resource isDirectory (Application.java, Generic-src.zip ~:368-371), caught by getApiSnapshotFile -> null -> missing_base. Model's Path.is_file() gate is the equivalent check.

files.patchverdiffs: a regular file, not a directory

cases.note: patchverdiffs present as a regular FILE: the source's per-patch probe builds 'patchverdiffs/go1.21.x.json.diff' under a non-directory and finds nothing -> null -> base only (:128-131). Model enumerates diff_dir and must treat NotADirectoryError like absence, not crash.
